100 Years Ago Today, This is What Was Happening ...

On August 12, 1926, the British Empire faced a significant crisis as a general strike continued to disrupt coal production, plunging the nation into economic turmoil. In the U.S., a severe drought affected vast agricultural areas, raising fears of food shortages. Meanwhile, in the world of entertainment, the successful silent film "The Jazz Singer" hinted at the future of cinema, paving the way for talking pictures.
